target_customer: Product designers at software companies who want to build working prototypes with a coding agent
problem: Designers are moving from drawing to building, but canvas design tools are made for drawing and general coding agents are made for engineers.
business_model: Software subscription for a designer-focused coding agent (pricing not published; early access alpha)
product_category: AI coding agent and IDE for designers

founders.name: Maayan Albert
education: Carnegie Mellon University, Bachelor's in Design and CS
founders.background_notes: YC page says she built an IDE for computational artists that was published at CHI. The YC launch post mentions an unnamed co-founder.

competitors.name: MagicPath
competitors.what: AI design canvas where designers and external coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) work in one session
competitors.traction_then: MagicPath 2.0 followed in May 2026; Pro plan from $21 per month on annual billing

competitors.name: Figma Make
competitors.what: Prompt to prototype inside Figma, needs a completed Figma design
competitors.traction_then: listed as a leading option in 2026 comparison roundups

competitors.name: Lovable
competitors.what: General prompt to full app builder, no design work needed
competitors.traction_then: usual pick for quick full-stack apps in 2026 roundups

competitors.name: Magic Patterns
competitors.what: AI prototyping tool for product teams

technical_complexity.rationale: Wrapping frontier coding models in a designer-oriented agent with sharing and idea exploration is standard engineering with hard UX parts; it is rebuilt from scratch per the YC page, but no proprietary model work is described.

defensibility.rationale: Several funded design-to-code tools existed by the 2026 batch and the product depends on third party models, so features are copyable quickly. Backers and designer taste are the only visible edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not yet known. Figma Make and MagicPath already occupied the wedge when the batch started in 2026.

market_need_then: The YC page and site argue designers are becoming builders. Evidence of demand is the number of 2026 design to code tools and comparison articles; no usage data for Proto was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses prototypes.fun rather than a proto.com style domain; no purchase story found.

identity.visual_style: Minimal site styled like a classic desktop menu bar (File, Edit, View, Special) with draggable portrait cards for backers.
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and promotional, for example promising to unlock your full creative potential.

branding.brand_signature: Retro desktop menu bar and backer portrait cards on the landing page
branding.community_and_virality: Landing page lists design-world backers (Soleio, David Hoang, Stephen Haney and others) as social proof; no independent community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Very early alpha. The name is generic and collides with Proto.io and other products named Proto, and searches found no coverage of the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Proto joined YC in the Fall 2026 batch as a two person team building a coding agent for designers. It is too early for an outcome. The wedge is real but crowded, with MagicPath, Figma Make and Lovable already serving designers, so the open question is whether a designer-native agent with strong sharing and idea exploration can beat those and the general coding agents.
notes: Outcome searches found nothing (company is months old). Dealroom lists a $125k seed for a San Francisco company called Proto but the entry is sparse and unconfirmed, so no round is recorded. The YC standard deal is not recorded as a round. Co-founder is unnamed in sources. Completeness pass: the 125K seed rests on Dealroom alone; date and investors unknown, founder names not matched.
